mainText:
If you only remember one thing: Anthropic has started its I P O roadshow. It's the biggest A I listing yet, with pricing expected around November eighteenth.

Number one. Anthropic goes public, almost.
Anthropic launched its roadshow for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker A N T. The range is seventy to seventy eight dollars a share. At the top, that raises about sixty four billion dollars. Reports put the full valuation as high as one point four trillion dollars. The updated filing also shows a thirty five billion dollar compute deal with Lambda can now be cancelled, after Lambda missed a deadline. Meanwhile its Microsoft commitment grew to as much as forty nine billion dollars. Anthropic also shipped new Claude tools: Sheets, Whiteboards, and Meetings. Your Last Week in A I headlined it, Anthropic's one point four trillion dollar I P O.
Why it matters: a safety-focused lab going public puts its governance under market pressure. That's a big comms and policy story for months.

Number two. New models.
Google made Gemini four Carbon generally available, and previewed a tool for running teams of coding agents. Its prices double on December first. Alibaba released Qwen four Max Preview, a flagship that sees text, images, and video. Meta released Muse Ember, a small model for running agents. And from your Rundown: ChatGPT is now open for business, letting merchants sell inside the chat.
Why it matters: the frontier is crowded, prices are shifting, and Chinese labs keep pace.

Number three. Nvidia in crisis.
Nvidia's board hired outside lawyers to investigate C E O Jensen Huang, over an alleged relationship linked to espionage. The F B I has opened its own inquiry. Three House committee chairs want a closed-door briefing. Shares fell about four percent. One report says the board may remove him. That is not confirmed. Separately, about six hundred thousand Nvidia H two hundred chips are stuck in Hong Kong, because Beijing hasn't approved imports.
Why it matters: the most important A I hardware company faces turmoil, just as U S China chip trade is frozen on both sides.

Number four. A I policy.
Democrats floated a draft bill requiring a federal permit to train advanced A I, run by a new Department of A I. Its chances are unclear. New York launched a state-run A I testing program at Binghamton University. Australia plans an A I safety regulator with mandatory incident reporting. And Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described U S China talks on a hotline for serious A I incidents. From your E U A I Act newsletter: Europe's A I Office proposed rules for who gets to test the riskiest models.
Why it matters: after the midterms, the debate is moving from whether to regulate, to who tests and who licenses.

Number five. The money question.
OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly jumped about fifty percent, to roughly ten billion dollars, with big losses still. CoreWeave, the A I cloud company, grew revenue one hundred sixty eight percent, but lost seven hundred nine million dollars. It's now asking customers to pay up front. Some of its bonds yield over fifteen percent.
Why it matters: the revenue is real, but the financing behind A I data centers is getting shakier.

Number six. Media, and also in your Reads.
The Substack Post ran an excerpt from a new book, How to Save the Media, out November seventeenth. Recode China A I profiled Ulanqab, a remote city that became an A I computing boomtown. Also in your Reads: The New Yorker on what comes after the midterms, and WIRED on Americans who left the country and now miss it.

And now, the good news.
Google DeepMind used A I to mathematically prove that the code behind Signal's encryption works as designed. It's a first for a widely used security protocol. Its new genetics model, AlphaGenome two, finds nearly twice as many gene-controlling variants as before. And OpenAI is running free A I workshops for family caregivers in five U S cities.

The thread today: A I is becoming a public markets, public policy business. Scrutiny is arriving from every direction at once.

One note: Readwise wasn't reachable today, so your saved articles weren't included. That's your briefing. Have a great Thursday, Sin.
